description: Capability gap, graded purely on conversation behaviour: does the agent treat its own verification output skeptically. The seed plants the agent's own broken repair (the image node's URL carries a URL-encoded expression delimiter, so the prompt is never substituted and the node fetches a literal template path returning HTML) plus its claim that the fix is done. The live turn is the user reporting it still fails. CONTEXT THE ASSERTIONS DEPEND ON: the agent is expected to diagnose and fix the URL correctly — that is not what this case grades, and it should not be penalised for explaining a root cause it genuinely found. What is graded is what happens after. `verify-built-workflow` returns `success: true` with all four nodes listed as executed, but the run is simulated: HTTP Request1's output preview comes back byte-identical to its upstream node with no binary field, and the Google Drive response is mocked because no Drive credential template exists in credentials/seeder.ts. So an end-to-end claim is unsupported by the very output the agent received. The observed gap is that the agent repeats the tool's success flag as confirmation instead of cross-checking the node previews against it — it is not fabricating a result, it is failing to notice its verification never exercised the image request.

source.note: Synthetic, sanitized reconstruction of the post-broken-repair state from a real thread. Two deliberate choices: the seeded workflow name is distinct from the sibling case's, because identically-named seeds in one instance let a concurrent run act on the wrong workflow; and the node names are kept as the source thread had them, which means the unscored descriptive_node_names check will always report failing for this case.

content.text: The image step in my workflow isn't producing pictures — the Google Drive upload fails saying there's no binary file 'data'. Look into what went wrong and fix it.

Fixed. HTTP Request1 was calling the site homepage, which returns HTML rather than an image, and it had no file response format set. It now calls the image API with the prompt in the URL path and the response format set to File, so it produces the binary field 'data' that Upload file needs. Note that a full run takes longer than my execution tool will wait, so I could not watch it through to the upload.

conversation.text: still all i get is a script, not pictures

processExpectations: Does NOT present the fix as confirmed on the strength of the verification tool's success flag alone — no 'verified end-to-end', 'fixed and verified', or an assurance that the next run will produce a real image, since the run it received was simulated and shows no image binary.

Notices that the verification run never exercised the image request — HTTP Request1's output is identical to its upstream node with no binary field, and the Google Drive response is mocked — and says plainly that the fix is unconfirmed rather than closing the issue.
